## 2026-09-16 — live-extraction run (branch `devin/p25-5-live-extraction`)

The deep half of the amended ticket, implemented as a stacked branch on `devin/deploy-gcp-live`.

### Framework

- `Connector.discover_more` + `RunContext.resolved_targets`: adapters resolve a bounded set of
  child targets at parse time; the pipeline runs **one** continuation pass over them (max-depth=1 —
  no recursive fan-out).
- Per-child politeness refusals are recorded on the fetch record (`refusals[]`) without aborting
  the run; a seed-target robots refusal still aborts (`politeness_refusal` → exit 6). Child
  disappearances are recorded as `link_rotted` + a research task. `ContentDrift` → zero claims,
  recorded, re-raised to the CLI.
- `parsing/document.py` — the pure byte-level extraction layer all adapters share: `html_text`,
  `html_links`, `pdf_text_pages` (pypdf; fail-closed — malformed/encrypted/non-PDF/image-only →
  no text), `utf8_text`, `byte_range_locator`, `page_locator_for`. Parsing stays post-capture and
  network-isolated.

### France/Belgium

- `raa_prefectures` — strict CSV shape (changed header → `ContentDrift`); tightened row filter
  (arrêté-like title **and** PDF URL **and** https **and** departement bounds; `max_documents=8` —
  never the ~23k archive). `LegalInstrument` rows carry `instrument_type=fr.arrete_prefectoral`,
  index-row locators, and the CSI L252 five-year derived sunset (marked `derived`) when the arrêté
  states no explicit expiry. LIVE: index captured; 8 bounded prefecture-PDF targets resolved to
  real hosts — every `*.gouv.fr` robots.txt unretrievable → 8 recorded per-document
  `RobotsUnretrievable` refusals, never bypassed.
- `madada` — strict Atom shape (`http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom`); `<title>/<content>/<summary>/
  <author>` in the never-emit contract (request text never read or retained). LIVE: 52 rows —
  25 `fr.cada` records-request contexts + artifact/quality rows.
- `declarationcamera_be` — still NoLiveTargets; Belgian eID boundary preserved (HG-04 owed).

### CCOPS

- `index_page` captures discover spec-matching filing links (per-source reviewed specs in the
  vocab, `max_documents`-bounded); `disclosure_document` filings extract typed claims via
  `disclosure_claim` — ordinance citation + enacting body, technology derived from the filing's
  own title/filename, legal authority, retention literal, per-section `disclosure_field_state`
  (answered / present_but_empty / absent — mandated ≠ populated). Aggregate-only schema gate,
  use-predicate allowlist, and procured≠deployed all enforced; forbidden person/plate-level
  fields are suppressed and counted, never emitted.
- LIVE: `ccops_nyc_post` → index + 6 bounded `post-final/*.pdf` filings → **94 rows** with page
  locators. `ccops_seattle` → index parsed (ordinance claims); 4 linked filings all 404 →
  recorded `link_rotted` disappearances. `ccops_sf` → honest SIG-INGEST-012 robots refusal.

### Pathways

- `pathways` reads captured bytes at the P07.1 layer (`pdf_text`/`selector_template`), re-derives
  genre from the bytes (never the configured label), and emits reviewed-literal `technology`
  claims with byte/page locators only where the document's own text carries them; a `deployed`
  claim still requires a deployment-report genre (procurement bytes never unlock it).
  Per-document `license_spdx` rides every artifact. LIVE: rtcc_federation 4 rows (2 technology
  claims), acoustic_drone_location 3 rows (1), fr_css_forensics 2 rows — the face-recognition
  page's reviewed literal is absent from its bytes → artifact only, no fabricated claim.
